title: dataref reads a db: address through db_domain's client
intention: A dataref reads a db: address: db:///cairn/<table>/<primary-key value>#<column> gives that row's column as text, through db_domain's published client, never a second dial to 5432, and caching nothing.
why: Measured 2026-11-10: cairn/tools/dataref/dataref.py line 56 refuses every db: address ('db: is read through db_domain's own client (outline 17.28.3), which is not built yet'), so secret:db:///cairn/t/row#token, the outline's own example in 17.28.1.4, raises. The client it names exists and reads.
traces_to: Outline 17.28.1.1 (db:///cairn/table/row is the database), 17.28.1.4 (secret:db:///cairn/t/row#token), 17.28.3 (a db: address is read through db_domain's own client, never a second dial to 5432), 17.28.4 (a db Dataref does not cache until a measured need asks), 17.28.5 (a miss is loud). Ticket 060d2146618c built the file roots and named db: next. RULE 1, Law 7.
how: In cairn/tools/dataref/dataref.py, a db: address parses to (database, table, key, item); the read finds the table's one primary-key column in information_schema and selects the row through cairn/devices/db_domain/tools/client/store.py's read(), every time (17.28.4: a db Dataref does not cache). #column gives that column as text; #column/a/b walks into a json column as into a json file; no # gives the whole row as json. Secret wraps it as it wraps a file. Every miss is a DatarefMiss naming the address.

clauses.claim: db:///cairn/<table>/<key>#<column> gives that row's column as text, a text column as written and an integer as its digits; with no # it gives the whole row as a json object
#<column>/a/b walks into a json column as into a json file, a list index included

Secret('secret:db:///cairn/<table>/<key>#<column>') shows stars in str, repr and an f-string and its .secret is the value; after the row is updated, the next .secret and the next Dataref .value read the new value

a missing row, a missing column, a missing table, a database other than cairn, a NULL column, an address with no row, and an address naming a host each raise DatarefMiss naming the address, with no value from the table in the message and no chained exception
cairn/tools/dataref/dataref.py imports no database driver and no socket: its only way to Postgres is cairn/devices/db_domain/tools/client/store.py

falsifier.wrong_intent: dataref reaches Postgres any way but db_domain's client

decisions.text: D1: cairn/tools/dataref/dataref.py: NOT_YET loses db. A db: address with no host parses its path as /<database>/<table>/<key> (each segment url-unquoted; fewer than three, or a database other than store.DB_NAME, is a miss naming the address) and its # into names. Every read (a Dataref .value, a Secret .secret) imports the store client lazily, finds the table's primary-key column with store.query over information_schema.table_constraints and key_column_usage (no table, or no single-column key, is a miss), and reads with store.read(table, where='"<key column>"::text = %s', params=(key,)). No row is a miss. No # gives json.dumps of the row (default=str). #<column> gives a str column as is, None as a miss, a dict or list as json.dumps, anything else as str(); further names walk the column's json the way the json file walk does. reads counts each read; nothing is cached. A connection failure is a miss naming the address, never chained. Its path attribute is None. The docstring's READ-ONLY paragraph says db: is built.

D2: through the artifact door, cairn/tools/dataref/intention+why.json's fields that say db: is not built say it reads through cairn.devices.db_domain.tools.client.store (ticket eb16737ff959); its proof list gains cairn/tools/dataref/proofs/test_dataref_reads_db.py.

D3: the proof cairn/tools/dataref/proofs/test_dataref_reads_db.py, red-first, one tooth per clause, PROVES {'eb16737ff959': {'1': ..., '5': ...}}. It mints a scratch table through store.scratch (owner dataref; columns id text primary key, token text, n integer, j jsonb, gone text), writes one row with a random token through store.write, and drops it on exit. Tooth 5 reads the module's ast.

out: a db: address naming a host (17.28.1.2, over the bus)

measured.saw: db: refuses by name; 44 tables carry a primary key, all single-column
measured.how: read cairn/tools/dataref/dataref.py; ran store.query over information_schema for primary keys
